newsitem.title: USA: Washington state voters pass $425 mln stadium.
newsitem.headline: Washington state voters pass $425 mln stadium.

text.p: A $425 million football stadium measure has extended its lead in a cliffhanger election pitting cash-strapped opponents against the vast resources of a billionaire businessman, officials said Sunday.
Stadium supporters, backed by billionaire Paul Allen, were leading by nearly 35,000 votes, according to the latest returns. Only 25,000 ballots are left to be counted.
The results were expected to be certified Tuesday.

The proposal would provide about $325 million in public money for a 72,000-seat open-air stadium to house the Seattle Seahawks. Allen, co-founder of Microsoft Corp and owner of the NBA Portland Trail Blazers, would invest an additional $100 million in the project.

Allen, worth more than $13 billion, offered to buy the Seahawks -- but only if the stadium referendum was approved. The new stadium, which would open in 2002, would replace the aging Kingdome, an indoor facility that would be demolished.

The stadium financing package would include $101 million from existing sales taxes, $127 million from lottery games, $56 million in stadium admissions and parking taxes, and $40 million in hotel room taxes.
The state would issue up to $300 million of bonds to pay for site acquisition, design and construction of the stadium and an exhibition center.
